prompt:
I need the front end for Flipledger. A personal analysis tool for weekend resellers who thrift and resell secondhand goods and want to understand which finds actually pay off.

Who's using it: Gus Ferreira, a high-school chemistry teacher who has spent three years buying vintage film cameras and lenses at estate sales and thrift stores, cleaning them up and reselling them online. It's a hobby that funds itself, and he wants to know whether it really does.

What they're doing right now: His spare room is overflowing and his partner wants half of it back, so this winter Gus is deciding what to stop buying. He has just imported his full sales history. He suspects that medium-format cameras make most of his profit while cheap point-and-shoots eat his weekends. He wants to see profit against hours spent and days to sell for each category and platform. He also wants to know whether his price cuts after 30 days actually helped, and to drill into the outliers, like the lens that sat for 11 months.

What's in the system at this point: 612 items acquired from Oct 2023 to Nov 2026: 488 sold, 97 still listed, 27 kept or written off. Each item records the category (35mm SLR 214, point-and-shoot 171, medium format 58, lenses 139, accessories 30), brand and model, source (estate sale, thrift, flea market, online lot), purchase price (1–220), date acquired, repair or cleaning hours logged (0–6.5), parts cost, listing platform (two marketplaces and one camera forum), list date, price changes with dates, sale price, platform fees (8–13%), shipping cost, sale date and buyer feedback. Totals so far: revenue 41,380, cost of goods 12,950, fees and shipping 6,210, 1,140 hours logged. Example outlier: a Soviet 85 mm portrait lens bought for 15, listed Dec 2025 at 180, cut three times, sold Nov 2026 for 95.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
